storyInfo: On the eve of the battle, Antosha tells Ukusik his story and entrusts the letters to her. After Ukusik falls asleep, Matvey leaves her to Sonya. Pavlovich receives some special 'help'.

attributes.content: No, can't write that.
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: 'Cleanse the gray streets with snow water'? 'Bring a wet pack of smokes'? No, that's not right either!
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: By the pale moonlight he gazes upon the heavily-marked draft, lamenting his lack of inspiration. This poem was worse than his fellow student's sleep-talking on the bunk next to him.
The Unbound camp is eerily quiet after the fire, the winter wind like a blunt knife cutting upon the young people's faces.
The ones that still have strength left whisper to each other, wrapping themselves in moldy jackets, looking like mounds of dirt under the dark night, occasionally laughing softly.
...Give every star a name to remember.
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: Give those who want to forget a cup of cheap spirits.
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: Give me...
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: Give me a one-way ticket to spring...
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: Let me live in the wind that blows upon the tundra.
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: Boo—
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: You again... I swear, one of these days, I'll be immune to your pranks.
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: You're writing those stupid poems again, Yura.
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: They are not stupid poems! I put my heart and soul in them. Besides, you can't even read them.
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: Don't want to. People who can read, people like you, always have such sullen looks on your faces.
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Matvey's taught me how to read addresses. At the end of the day, whatever you guys are writing, I'm the one who has to deliver it for you.
attributes.name: Ukusik
Ukusik
attributes.content: Say it, Yura. Which girl am I delivering to this time?

attributes.name: Ukusik
attributes.content: Ouch—
This is for you, little brat!
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: You hit me! I'm taking this away so that you don't get to write it!
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Come on, it's just a roll of paper, it can't have hurt all that much... but you can have it, if you want.
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: This time... I'm writing for everyone. Including you.
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: You're so weird... I'll put it in my bag, then.
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Never mind that, Ukusik.
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: You should talk to Antosha. I think he has a lot of letters there.
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: Doesn't he eat and spend the nights with you guys? Why don't I see him around?
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Who knows? He's in there. Ask him for me.
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: And pull that jacket tighter. He'll yell at us if you catch a cold.
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: Hm? He never yells at me.
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Bye, Yura.
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: That's because we are the ones he yells at, little brat...
attributes.name: Yura

attributes.content: I'm here, Antosha.
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: No need to be so loud every time, Ukusik.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: Yura said you've got letters to give to me. Where?
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Yes. There's quite a lot.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: He goes to the corner and picks up a thick stack of letters.
Oh, bother... lemme see.
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: This one's for No. 34 Odoyev Old Street? The second is No. 15 Zheleznaya Left Bank Street, the third one to the spice market...
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Wait, did you write all these letters, Antosha? What are these places?
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: No. 34 Odoyev Old Street is Yura's home, then Lev's and Vissarion's...
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: I wrote one for everyone. We'll see how many you'll need to deliver after we take that magistrate down.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: If any fall tomorrow... I don't want their families to learn about them from casualty reports.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: When did you memorize all this?
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: When someone entrusts their life to me, I must know where it comes from... I can never forget it.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: You remember how I asked where you came from?
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: You just didn't expect me to be an orphan with no name.
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Hey, what's that look on your face?
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: I've never been as depressed as you look, and I'm the one who had no parents and no name. Besides, I saved you a piece of paper.
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Say, are you and Matvey's letters in this pile too?
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Mine, perhaps, but certainly not his.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: Matvey?
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: We usually meet before we do something big.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: Do you have beer?
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: Last two bottles. Someone stuffed them under a pile of rotten vegetables, but List sniffed them out while we were preparing equipment.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: ...Give me one.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: Can I try? I'm thirsty—
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: How old do you think you are? Forget it.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: Zhopa!
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Matvey pats her on the head, then sits beside Antosha and gives him a bottle.
Why did you say Antosha won't write home?
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Why does he have me deliver letters if he thinks he won't die? Is he scared?
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Hah, of course not...
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: He hasn't had any contact with his family for a long time.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: Antosha?
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: It's alright. All in the past now.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: The subject of Antosha came up in a conversation with someone else, not long after we met.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: I accidentally called him Anton Shestov, which he happened to overhear. He was in a sullen mood for a month afterwards.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: Anton Shestov? Sounds like some important noble.
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: I abandoned the name and the one who gave it to me before I went to university.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: I expect they're more relieved to be rid of a troublemaking traitor than saddened by the loss of a son.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: I've never heard about Antosha's family before...
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Were they mean to you?
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: My grandfather killed the landlord who oppressed him and returned home a count.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: He was the 'hero' that I wanted to grow up to be, so I imitated the stories, ate and lived with the serfs, and made friends with all the peasant servants.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: I didn't care that my family didn't think it was proper. I thought that at least my grandfather would understand.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: Until I grew older and wiser...
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: When an old serf accidentally knocked him over, my grandfather forced the man to strangle the pet musbeast he had raised for years with his own hands, right in front of us.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: Antosha, you don't have to talk about this—
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: Still, I continued to fantasize... until that night when my grandfather held a great feast to celebrate my acceptance into a Grypherburg university.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: A maid around the same age as me sneaked into the kitchen and took some food, hoping to give her mother and brother a treat.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: The police wanted to take her, but my grandfather stopped them.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: He said with a laugh, 'Today is a good day. I want everyone to be happy for my grandson's glory.'
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: A couple of days later, I saw a body by the side of the road as I was traveling to Grypherburg. There were bloody whip marks all over her.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: The butler told me that the police would only keep her in jail for a few days. Only the noble right of corporal punishment could 'teach her a real lesson'.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: But it was I who learned the lesson. I see the flies crawling over her eyelashes whenever I close my eyes.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: That was when I learned that oppression will persist as long as the nobility does, as long as the only outcome of any struggle is to turn different people into nobles.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: Let me tell you this, Antosha.
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: The worst has already passed... we'll win.
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Tomorrow, by tomorrow, I—
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: She slurs the last few words and passes out on Matvey's shoulder.
With a start, Antosha snatches the bottle from Ukusik's arms. It is completely empty.
Ukusik—and I was wondering how you learned to comfort a man like that.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: You stole my booze... why didn't you watch her, Matvey?
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: For the better, I suppose... don't wake her. I was just thinking about how to get her to leave.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: It's time to take her away.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: But you know that where we're going...
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: Heh...
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: I'll help.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: So... did you write a letter for me too?
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: There's no need. I trust you.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: I had Ukusik take a letter to my mother a little while back, when she could still get out through the hole.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: What did you write?
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: 'We'll be out of this place and back in the city in ten days, at most.'
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: It's time to go, my friend.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: Remember to come back.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: Matvey closes his eyes and nods.
Good night, Matvey...
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: See you at dawn.
attributes.name: Antosha

attributes.content: How long is it gonna take, Rosalind? You've been fiddling with that all night.
attributes.name: Excited Student

attributes.content: It's a guitar, not some rag doll.
attributes.name: Leto

attributes.content: You dug this out of the trash heap without a single working peg. No way to fix this fast.
attributes.name: Leto

attributes.content: Well, tomorrow's the big day. We'll take all the notes you can give us.
attributes.name: Excited Student

attributes.content: Hmph... give me the clamps.
attributes.name: Leto

attributes.content: ...Have you checked everything?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Yes. The building is structurally sound. The wounded will be safe there.
attributes.name: Cautious Student

attributes.content: Good. Talk to Mykola and double-check the assignments on both sides of the street.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: No mistakes, you understand?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Yes, ma'am!
attributes.name: Cautious Student

attributes.content: ...Bad timing, Sonya?
Matvey?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: What are you doing here? Did something happen on your side? Anything we can do?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Thanks, but we're fine.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: The way Antosha was talking back there... he wouldn't come to you even if he was starving to death, that stubborn hard-head.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: I came because of her.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: He turns sideways and shows the snoring girl behind him.
She smells of...
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: She got into the beer while we weren't looking.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: I want to give her to you. Given the manpower and battle plans, she'll be safer with your group.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: Rosalind still has a few mats. Go and talk to her.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Phew...
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: Thank you. I mean it.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: I was afraid that after your argument...
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: He may be ice cold... but we have to admit you are all great warriors.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: ...Antosha used to be more passionate.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: He was a strange one from the day I met him. He had the demeanor of a great noble, but he kept pestering our teacher about where he could pick up odd jobs.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: He assisted the professor in writing essays that criticized aristocratic politics. The council at the time did not punish them; they even promoted the professor to school inspector.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: That day, Antosha took my hands and said there was hope for Ursus at least. People will no longer suffer, and we will all be free.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: We planted a cherry tree in the school garden to celebrate the occasion.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: Until our newspaper was shut down, and the professor died for us...
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: You...
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: We were expelled. The professor shouldered most of the responsibility in exchange for an 'amnesty' towards us.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: The night before we left school, Antosha sat in front of the cherry tree, stroking its leafless branches. He sat there all night.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: I should find Rosalind. Thank you again.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: One moment, Matvey.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: You said it was safer to stay here...
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Why don't you stay?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: No, I made a promise tonight.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: ...Or long before that, perhaps.
attributes.name: Matvey

attributes.content: Did it work?
attributes.name: Excited Student

attributes.content: Let me try.
attributes.name: Leto

attributes.content: Not quite in tune, but at least it makes a sound now.
attributes.name: Leto

attributes.content: Yay! I knew you were a genius, Rosalind!
attributes.name: Excited Student

attributes.content: NOW you try to sweet-talk me. How about you spend that time thinking what you want to hear?
attributes.name: Leto

attributes.content: Okay... 'On the Old River'? Or some Leithanian song...
attributes.name: Excited Student

attributes.content: Hmph, I'm not playing that soft sentimental stuff.
attributes.name: Leto

attributes.content: How about I improvise a few chords, and you guys sing something that fits the scene?
attributes.name: Leto

attributes.content: Isn't that a bit hard?
attributes.name: Excited Student

attributes.content: What did you take all those literature courses for? Start thinking about the lyrics, because here I go.
attributes.name: Leto

attributes.content: One, two, three...
attributes.name: Leto

attributes.content: Step over cobwebs of iron♪
Strip the night's hard shell♪
Come, brothers and sisters♪
The spring sprout will break through the frozen soil♪
Instead of waiting for a false dawn in the snow♪
Mm... this sound...
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: ...Matvey?
attributes.name: Ukusik

attributes.content: Still no news?
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: How much time do you think has already passed?!
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: We've secured the sentry turrets on the two roads, but—
attributes.name: Security Team Captain

attributes.content: Was I asking about the turrets? I'm talking about reinforcements and supplies!
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: What about the crossbows that Daniila Treplev promised me? What about the artillery? The tanks? The armies?
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: I sent him a thousand letters, and he hasn't written a single word back!
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: Please, calm down, sir. The few of us here are well-equipped with crossbows and emergency catapult systems. We can assure your safety.
attributes.name: Security Team Captain

attributes.content: 'Calm down'? 'The few of us'?
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: Are you telling me that I hired you so that I can pay your wages? You think they'll just let me go if I run away? How's that any different from being dead?
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: If you want your money, 'captain', you'd better do your jobs and kill those troublemakers!
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: But you only had the budget for the few of us, some of whom you sent to help Gromov, while there are hundreds of them—
attributes.name: Security Team Captain

attributes.content: I don't need you to tell me! I can hear them singing through my window!
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: They're singing my elegy!
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: ...Who are you?
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: Good evening, magistrate. I am Captain Chicherin.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: You must have plenty of supplies here, to turn the heat up so high that you are sweating so much.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: You... no, no. You bring help from Duke Treplev? Please, take a seat.
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: No, His Grace is no longer interested in Katorga Raion.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: Why?!
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: It is not my place to guess at His Grace's intentions.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: However, while he did not send me, it is true that I am here to support you.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: Yes... I knew the empire would reward my loyalty for my service in Katorga.
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: How many men do you have? How many heavy weapons? You can set them up at once. Put a cannon in this room, for all I care!
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: I'm afraid you misunderstood.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: I do not have men. My superior assigned me thirty guards, and no heavy weapons.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: What?!
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: However, he has prepared this for you.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: The officer takes out a black, palm-sized box and hands it to Pavlovich.
It is an encrypted military terminal connected directly to an artillery position outside the city.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: If you are truly desperate... press the red button, and we will provide 'suitable' firepower coverage.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: What do you mean by 'suitable'? I want to level the whole district.
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: That would be impossible. Every shell has a cost, and every block is an asset, even in Katorga Raion.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: What about Originium bolts? Explosives? Surely you could carry those?
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: All here.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: Only then does Pavlovich notice that the officer is carrying two small briefcases.
This is to avoid the weapons falling into the hands of the rioters. After all, the supplies that were given to you have been taken by the students. We can only risk so much.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: I... I did your dirty work, and you people just...
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: Your sponsors have shown plenty of good will by putting thirty elite men at your disposal.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: Besides, I believe you underestimate the 'weapon' in your hands. Press it, and Ursus will bestow upon you the supreme 'glory'...
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: The magistrate ponders the meaning of these words as he clutches the cold communicator in his sweaty palm.
Yes... I cannot abandon hope... they will help me, I can beat that rabble...
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: Guards!
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: You called, sir?
attributes.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Thug

attributes.content: How many of you are still combat-ready?
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: Three to four hundred, I think?
attributes.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Thug

attributes.content: As long as it's more than the other side. Get them warmed up. I'll give them their revenge for Gromov!
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: Aye, sir!
attributes.name: 'Sixteen Warriors' Thug

attributes.content: You, plant explosives at the door. If they dare to come in, we'll all go and see Igor Velikiy together!
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: Uh...
attributes.name: Security Team Captain

attributes.content: As for you, Captain, I need you to deal with the Unbound.
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: Do not underestimate them. I've been fighting them for two months. They are few in number, but they are experienced.
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: More importantly, they kill any nobles they see on sight... harbor no fantasies about them. The council would not want to let them out.
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: Yes.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: If my ears do not deceive me... someone is coming.
attributes.name: Ursine Officer

attributes.content: ...Let's go.
attributes.name: Pavlovich

attributes.content: It's time to teach these brats a lesson.
attributes.name: Pavlovich
